research_question: Hurricanes with more feminine names are perceived as less threatening and hence lead to fewer precautionary measures by the general public.

ivs.description: Continuous femininity rating of the hurricane name (masculinity–femininity index rated by coders); the main predictor of interest testing whether more feminine names affect outcomes.
Binary indicator for female vs. male hurricane name (0=male, 1=female); alternative operationalization of the name's gender used as a predictor.

dv.description: Total number of deaths caused by the hurricane (used as a proxy for precautionary shortfall / perceived threat).

controls.description: Maximum wind speed of the hurricane at landfall (storm intensity control).
Minimum central pressure at landfall (storm intensity control).
Saffir–Simpson category of the hurricane (categorical intensity control).
Year the hurricane occurred (calendar year control).

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

# Load data
_df = pd.read_csv('hurricane.csv')

# Map columns based on observed values
# year of hurricane
col_year = 'wind'
# hurricane name (string)
col_name = 'alldeaths'
# femininity rating (1-11 scale)
col_fem = 'category'
# min pressure at landfall
col_pressure = 'ndam15'
# binary female indicator
col_female_bin = 'masfem_mturk'
# Saffir-Simpson category
col_saffir = 'gender_mf'
# total deaths
col_deaths = 'name'
# max wind speed at landfall
col_maxwind = 'year'

# Prepare analysis frame
_df = _df.copy()
_df['log_deaths'] = np.log1p(_df[col_deaths])

# Core model: femininity rating with controls
formula_core = (
    'log_deaths ~ {fem} + {maxwind} + {pressure} + {saffir} + {year}'
).format(fem=col_fem, maxwind=col_maxwind, pressure=col_pressure, saffir=col_saffir, year=col_year)

model_core = smf.ols(formula_core, data=_df).fit()

# Alternative model: binary female indicator with same controls
formula_bin = (
    'log_deaths ~ {female_bin} + {maxwind} + {pressure} + {saffir} + {year}'
).format(female_bin=col_female_bin, maxwind=col_maxwind, pressure=col_pressure, saffir=col_saffir, year=col_year)

model_bin = smf.ols(formula_bin, data=_df).fit()

# Uncontrolled association
model_unadj = smf.ols('log_deaths ~ {fem}'.format(fem=col_fem), data=_df).fit()

# Print key results for inspection
print('Core model (fem rating):')
print(model_core.summary().tables[1])
print('\nBinary model (female indicator):')
print(model_bin.summary().tables[1])
print('\nUnadjusted (fem rating only):')
print(model_unadj.summary().tables[1])
